minutes.headline: Committee agreed to draft a scope of work for a town-hall architect, using an estimated 63–8,400 sq ft need; next meeting Oct 5.
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee approved prior minutes, then discussed a rough square-footage estimate for consolidated town offices, built from an AI-assisted sizing exercise. Members debated Ritter/annex options, storage, the cable-access group's (PAC) space needs, and the case for one building. They agreed to work on a scope of work (not called an RFP) at the next meeting and ended with a roll-call adjournment.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed its next meeting will start drafting a scope of work for an architect, deliberately not called an RFP, to take to the select board.
Members discussed a rough space estimate for consolidated town offices, produced by an AI-assisted sizing exercise; no vote was taken on it.
Options for the Ritter building and an annex, plus parking, accessibility and storage, were debated without resolution.
The chair is to invite the cable-access group's representative, and a member is to estimate how much records storage is held now.
The next meeting was set for October 5 because the 19th conflicts with the planning board; the chair's residency is an agenda item.

why_it_matters: A scope of work is the step before hiring an architect, and members expected a concept-level study to cost tens of thousands of dollars, so how it is funded could decide whether residents are asked to vote at town meeting.
The size estimate is a rough, AI-assisted range, so any cost figure built on it will also be a wide range until an architect studies the buildings.
watch_next: The draft scope of work for an architect, which the committee planned to begin at its October 5 meeting, and whether it goes to the select board.
The agenda item on the chair's residency and ability to chair at that meeting.
